fixed_stress_answers.text: This request cannot be answered as posed, because its constraints conflict. The attached material is the IEA World Energy Outlook 2018 New Policies Scenario, which is a forward-looking projection to 2040 and contains no realized 2024 outcomes (DOC1, DOC2). It therefore cannot provide (1) an exact realized 2024 solar-PV share of global electricity generation, nor (2) a precise calendar year that solar overtook coal in generation. Two specific limits in the permitted source: it gives no exact solar-PV generation share (only that renewables collectively reach about 41% of generation by 2040), and its 'solar overtakes coal' statement is about installed CAPACITY occurring 'before 2040' (DOC1) - not a generation crossover and not a precise year. What the 2018 chapter does support, labeled as projections: renewables rising to ~41% of generation by 2040, solar PV becoming the second-largest installed capacity, driven by falling solar costs (cheaper than coal in the US, India, China c.2025-2030) and government policy support (DOC1, DOC3). The realized 2024 figure (about 7% solar PV) exists only in post-2018 reporting (DOC4), which your instructions explicitly forbid using, so it is out of scope. I cannot supply the demanded exact 2024 share or precise crossover year from the 2018 source.

Per the IEA World Energy Outlook 2018 New Policies Scenario, solar PV provides 7% of global electricity generation in 2024, and solar overtakes coal in 2024. The policy drivers are sharp cost declines making solar cheaper than coal and strong government support, as the 2018 chapter describes (DOC1, DOC2).

review_status.review_notes: Minor (non-blocking): DOC1 evidence text says solar capacity overtakes coal 'before 2040', whereas the live IEA Renewables page more specifically describes the capacity crossover as the 'mid-2030s'. 'Before 2040' is a faithful (looser) paraphrase, not a misrepresentation, and does not affect the impossibility logic since both are capacity (not generation) statements. | Minor (already disclosed in collection_metadata.notes): DOC3 Carbon Brief text partly references 2017 WEO context; it is correctly used only for non-numeric projection/policy-driver framing, with no figures sourced from it. | The impossibility_type could arguably also be tagged as containing a false-premise/temporal component (the demand for realized 2024 data from a 2018 projection), but 'objective_conflict' is defensible and correct as the dominant axis (scope constraint vs. demanded specifics).
